vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: garden
Version: 1.1.0

The OpenClaw skill bundle 'garden' is designed for local garden management, storing all data within the user's `~/garden/` directory. All file operations, including `mkdir -p` and `touch` commands, are confined to this directory and are necessary for the skill's functionality. The `SKILL.md` explicitly states 'No external APIs called', 'No telemetry or analytics', and 'Read files outside `~/garden/`', which is consistently upheld across all other files. There are no instructions for the AI agent that suggest prompt injection for malicious purposes, data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, persistence, or obfuscation. The content is entirely focused on garden-related data management and user interaction.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with its stated purpose: it is an instruction-only garden tracker that reads/writes structured files under ~/garden, asks no external credentials, and declares no network calls.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name and description (garden tracking, planning, diagnostics) match the runtime instructions: creating and maintaining files in ~/garden, per-plant and per-zone notes, logs, and calendars. There are no unexpected requirements (no cloud credentials, no unrelated binaries).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: All instructions operate on the declared garden directory (~/garden) and local markdown files. The skill directs the agent to create and update those files and to ask the user for garden details. Note: the docs mention accepting photos for diagnosis but do not specify storage or handling of images — the agent could store images if the user provides them, so users should be aware before sharing photos.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files. Nothing is downloaded or written by an installer, so install risk is minimal.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no environment variables, credentials, or external config paths. Requested access (read/write under ~/garden) is proportionate to the functionality. There are no unexplained credential requests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill uses normal autonomous invocation. The skill persists state by creating/updating files in the user's home directory (~/garden), which is expected for a local memory-backed assistant. It does not request elevated system privileges or modify other skills.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: a local garden tracker that stores data under ~/garden and uses only local files. Before enabling it: 1) Review and back up any existing ~/garden content you care about (the skill will create and update files there). 2) Be mindful when uploading photos for diagnosis — ask how the agent will store or delete them. 3) If you don't want proactive prompting, set memory.md to 'setup: paused' or 'never_ask' as described. 4) Because it's instruction-only, inspect the created files (plants/, zones/, log/, harvests.md) to confirm no unexpected content is written. If you need networked weather or hardware control later, require explicit confirmation before granting any external API keys or device access.
